narrative:
The model predicts you have a 10% chance of failing your final year. While this is a low probability, the school has decided this risk is high enough to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction that you might fail is mainly driven by three key aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. Surprisingly, this actually pushes the model toward expecting you to fail. Among students who passed, having zero previous failures is the average, yet in your specific combination of circumstances the model sees this clean record as less protective than it appears. 

The second strongest influence is your reason for choosing this school: its strong reputation. This choice also pulls the prediction toward failing, even though 29% of students who succeeded picked the school for the same reason.

Third, your weekly study time of 5-10 hours works against you in the model’s eyes, nudging the outcome toward failure. Most students who passed studied only 2-5 hours, so your longer hours should be an advantage, but the model weighs this differently in your overall profile.

To improve, focus on making your study time more effective rather than simply longer. Build on your clean record by seeking early feedback from teachers, and reflect on whether the school’s reputation is truly helping your day-to-day learning. Taking the remedial courses seriously will give you extra support to turn this small risk into a clear success. (248 words)
